quizQuestions.prompt: What did two angels tell the disciples as Jesus ascended into a cloud before their eyes?
quizQuestions.explanation: "This same Jesus... shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go into heaven."

options.text: He would return in like manner as He left
He would never be seen again

quizQuestions.prompt: What sound accompanied the Holy Spirit's descent at Pentecost, filling the whole house?
quizQuestions.explanation: "A sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind."

quizQuestions.prompt: What new ability did the disciples receive at Pentecost that let people of many nations understand them?
quizQuestions.explanation: They were filled with the Holy Ghost and began to speak with other tongues (languages).

quizQuestions.prompt: How did the early believers in Jerusalem share their possessions, according to Acts 4?
quizQuestions.explanation: They held everything in common, and no one claimed private ownership of their goods.

options.text: They sold everything and left the city
They gave everything to the Romans

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to Ananias and Sapphira after they lied about the price they sold their land for?
quizQuestions.explanation: They both fell down dead after lying to the Holy Spirit about the sale.

quizQuestions.prompt: Why did the apostles appoint the first deacons, including Stephen, in Acts 6?
quizQuestions.explanation: A dispute arose over the daily distribution of food to widows, so seven men were appointed to serve.

options.text: To resolve a dispute over food distribution to widows

quizQuestions.prompt: Which official did Philip meet on a desert road and baptize after explaining a prophecy from Isaiah?
quizQuestions.explanation: Philip explained Isaiah's prophecy to an Ethiopian eunuch, an official of the queen, and baptized him.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which disciple did Peter raise from the dead in the town of Joppa?
quizQuestions.explanation: Peter raised Tabitha (also called Dorcas), known for her good works and charity.

quizQuestions.prompt: What vision did Peter have before meeting Cornelius, teaching him not to call any person common or unclean?
quizQuestions.explanation: Peter saw a vision of a sheet let down from heaven full of animals, told to "kill and eat."

options.text: A vision of a sheet full of animals
A vision of a burning altar
A vision of an empty tomb
A vision of a flooded city

quizQuestions.prompt: Which apostle, brother of John, was executed by King Herod, becoming the first apostle martyred?
quizQuestions.explanation: James, the brother of John, was killed with the sword by Herod.

quizQuestions.prompt: What major question did the Jerusalem Council in Acts 15 debate about Gentile converts?
quizQuestions.explanation: They debated whether Gentile believers needed to follow the Law of Moses, including circumcision.

options.text: Whether Gentiles must follow the Law of Moses
Whether to build a new temple
Whether to move the church to Rome

quizQuestions.prompt: Who was the seller of purple cloth, one of Paul's first converts in Europe, at Philippi?
quizQuestions.explanation: Lydia, a seller of purple, was baptized along with her household.

quizQuestions.prompt: In Athens, what altar inscription did Paul reference to introduce the true God to the philosophers at the Areopagus?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul referenced an altar inscribed "TO THE UNKNOWN GOD."

quizQuestions.prompt: What caused a major riot in Ephesus during Paul's ministry there?
quizQuestions.explanation: Silversmiths who made idols of the goddess Diana (Artemis) stirred up a riot, angry about lost business as people turned from idols.

options.text: Silversmiths angry about lost idol-making business
A dispute over the Temple in Jerusalem

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to a young man named Eutychus during an apostle's very long sermon in Troas?
quizQuestions.explanation: Eutychus fell asleep, fell from a window, and died, but Paul revived him.

options.text: He fell asleep, fell from a window, and was revived by Paul

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened when a viper bit Paul's hand after he was shipwrecked on Malta?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul suffered no harm, shaking the viper off into the fire, which amazed the local people.

options.text: He suffered no harm at all
His hand had to be removed

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Romans 3:23 say about the universal condition of humanity regarding sin?
quizQuestions.explanation: "For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God."

options.text: "All have sinned, and come short of the glory of God"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Romans 6:23 contrast sin's wages with God's free gift?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Romans 5:8 say demonstrates God's love toward us?
quizQuestions.explanation: "God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us."

options.text: Christ dying for us while we were still sinners

quizQuestions.prompt: What promise does Romans 8:28 give about how God works in the lives of those who love Him?
quizQuestions.explanation: "All things work together for good to them that love God."

options.text: All things work together for good

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Romans 8:38-39 declare can never separate believers from God's love?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul lists death, life, angels, powers, and more, declaring nothing can separate us from the love of God.

options.text: Only good deeds can maintain it
It can be lost through hardship

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Romans 10:9, what does Paul say is required for a person to be saved?
quizQuestions.explanation: Confess Jesus as Lord and believe God raised Him from the dead.

options.text: Confess Jesus as Lord and believe in His resurrection
Complete a set of good works

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Romans 12:1-2 urge believers to present as a "living sacrifice"?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul urges believers to present their bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Romans 12:2 say not to be, instead being transformed by the renewing of the mind?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind."

quizQuestions.prompt: Which church, one Paul had not yet personally visited when writing, is the book of Romans addressed to?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul wrote to the church at Rome, hoping to visit them.

quizQuestions.prompt: Romans is often considered Paul's most systematic theological letter. What core doctrine does it especially lay out?
quizQuestions.explanation: Romans systematically explains justification by faith, not by works of the law.

quizQuestions.prompt: In Romans 9-11, whose ongoing place in God's plan does Paul discuss at length as His chosen people?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul discusses Israel's place in God's redemptive plan across these chapters.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Romans 13:1 teach about governing authorities?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The powers that be are ordained of God," teaching submission to governing authority.

quizQuestions.prompt: What famous chapter in 1 Corinthians is often called "the love chapter"?
quizQuestions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13 describes the nature and priority of love (charity).

quizQuestions.prompt: According to 1 Corinthians 13:13, what three things remain, with which one being the greatest?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity."

options.text: Faith, hope, and charity -- the greatest is charity
Wisdom, power, and riches -- the greatest is power
Law, grace, and truth -- the greatest is law
Peace, joy, and patience -- the greatest is peace

quizQuestions.prompt: What major doctrine does 1 Corinthians 15 defend at length, central to the Christian faith?
quizQuestions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15 is a lengthy defense of the reality of Christ's and believers' resurrection.

quizQuestions.prompt: What image does Paul use in 1 Corinthians 12 to describe the church, with many parts working together?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul describes the church as a body with many members, each contributing different gifts.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 1 Corinthians 6:19 call the believer's body?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost."

options.text: The temple of the Holy Ghost

quizQuestions.prompt: What kinds of problems in the Corinthian church prompted Paul to write this corrective letter?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul addressed divisions, sexual immorality, lawsuits between believers, and disorder in worship.

options.text: Divisions, immorality, and disorder in worship

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Paul's account in 1 Corinthians 11 describe Jesus instituting the night He was betrayed?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul recounts the institution of the Lord's Supper, the bread and the cup.

quizQuestions.prompt: What activity does Paul compare the Christian life to in 1 Corinthians 9, involving discipline and a prize?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul compares it to running a race, disciplining the body like an athlete training for a prize.

quizQuestions.prompt: What farming image does Paul use in 1 Corinthians 3 to describe his and Apollos's ministry and its true source?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase."

options.text: Planting and watering, but God gives the increase

quizQuestions.prompt: What serious sin does Paul address in 1 Corinthians 5, saying even pagans wouldn't tolerate it?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul addresses a case of sexual immorality in the church, worse than what pagans practiced.

options.text: Sexual immorality tolerated in the church

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 2 Corinthians 5:17 say happens to someone who is "in Christ"?
quizQuestions.explanation: "If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away."

options.text: They must start over in the Law
They lose their past entirely from memory

quizQuestions.prompt: What did God tell Paul about his unnamed "thorn in the flesh" that he pleaded to have removed?
quizQuestions.explanation: "My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness."

options.text: "It will be removed within a year"
God gave no answer at all

quizQuestions.prompt: What kind of giver does 2 Corinthians 9:7 say God loves?
quizQuestions.explanation: "God loveth a cheerful giver."

options.text: A giver who gives in secret only

quizQuestions.prompt: What kinds of sufferings does Paul list in 2 Corinthians 11 to prove his apostolic credentials?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul lists shipwrecks, beatings, imprisonments, and many other hardships for the gospel.

quizQuestions.prompt: What comparison does 2 Corinthians 4 make between present suffering and future glory?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Our light affliction, which is but for a moment, worketh for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory."

options.text: Light, momentary affliction produces eternal glory
Glory comes only after death, never before

quizQuestions.prompt: What does 2 Corinthians 3:17 say is present where the Spirit of the Lord is?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty."

quizQuestions.prompt: What is notably more personal and defensive about the tone of 2 Corinthians, compared to Paul's first letter to them?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul defends his apostolic authority and character against false teachers who had been undermining him.

options.text: Paul defends his apostolic authority against false teachers
Paul announces a new set of laws

quizQuestions.prompt: What title does Paul give God in 2 Corinthians 1:3, right after calling Him "the Father of mercies"?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The God of all comfort."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Galatians 2:20 say about Paul's new identity after being spiritually "crucified" with his Savior?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me."

options.text: "I am no longer alive at all"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Galatians 5:22-23 call the qualities God produces in a believer's life?
quizQuestions.explanation: The fruit of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance.

quizQuestions.prompt: What unity does Galatians 3:28 declare exists among believers, regardless of ethnicity, status, or gender?
quizQuestions.explanation: "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus."

options.text: All are one in Christ Jesus
Only Jewish believers are truly equal
Only free men are fully included

quizQuestions.prompt: What false teaching was Paul specifically countering in his letter to the Galatians?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul countered legalism -- the idea that Gentile believers needed to keep the Mosaic law, including circumcision, to be saved.

options.text: That salvation required keeping the Mosaic law
That Jesus never rose from the dead
That the Old Testament should be discarded entirely

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Galatians 5:1 urge believers to stand fast in, now that they have been set free?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free."

options.text: A strict new set of rituals

quizQuestions.prompt: What encouragement does Galatians 6:9 give about doing good, even when tired?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not."

options.text: Don't grow weary; a harvest is coming

quizQuestions.prompt: How does Paul insist he received the gospel he preached, according to Galatians 1:11-12?
quizQuestions.explanation: Paul insists his gospel came directly by revelation from Jesus Christ, not from any man.

options.text: By direct revelation from Jesus Christ
From the other apostles' teaching alone
From years of rabbinic study alone

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Galatians 4:4 say about the timing of God sending His Son?
quizQuestions.explanation: "When the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

options.text: "When the fulness of the time was come"
"At the very end of all things"
